brief: GS Portfolio Strategy argues European equity resilience has been earnings-led: year-to-date EPS revisions explain almost 70% of relative sector moves, consensus expects 22% y/y EPS growth in 2H (15% ex-Energy), and breadth is normal with Europe's median stock beating the US and Asia. That resilience now meets a tougher rates backdrop: each 10bp rise in German Bund yields takes roughly 1.2% off the STOXX 600, and each 10bp of OAT/BTP spread widening versus Bunds costs 0.9% of Europe's P/E. Because of this, GS favors durable earnings and shareholder returns, citing Europe's 5.5% FCF yield versus 3.5% in the US and negative net equity supply from buybacks, and stays overweight Technology, Banks, Renewables, Defense and Capital-intensive sectors. The weekly recap: global equities fell 0.7%, Europe underperformed the US (-2.2% vs -0.3%) as Technology rose 1.4% while Financials fell 3.0%, rising yields hit Gold (-3.2%) while German Bunds returned 1.4% as a safe haven, and Brazilian equities rose 4.7% on growing Bolsonaro election-victory expectations.
